_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x19-rc-input.json and opened no other file, repository search, web page or API.

hints.reason: Avatar: The Last Airbender puts AIR in the title (Aang the airbender) and WATER is one of the four elements the Avatar bends; a familiar show with a clean click, though BALLOON (air/water balloon) is an equally good alternative.

pairs.pair_note: Solid pop-culture route; FIRE/EARTH on the board would compete, so placement matters.

hints.reason: One-armed bandit gives ARM, and the one-armed bandit is the casino slot machine, giving CASINO; a nice misdirect from the outlaw sense.
Cork is the bark of the cork oak (BARK) and Cork is a well-known Irish city and county (IRELAND); a true double meaning with a real aha.

Roman bath gives BATH instantly, but ENGLAND comes only via knowing the city of Bath's Roman baths or the general idea of Roman Britain, so the second side is soft for many U.S. players and ROMAN also pulls toward EMPIRE/NUMERAL.

pairs.pair_note: Lines are accurate; the doubt is whether U.S. players think of Bath the city. I could not find a clearly better one-word hint for this pair.

hints.reason: Angus beef gives BEEF and AC/DC's Angus Young gives YOUNG; classic rock is fair game and the switch from steak to guitarist is a real 'oh, nice'.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; YOUNG side depends on knowing AC/DC, which is widely known.

hints.reason: Minecraft's world is made of blocks (BLOCK) and zombies are one of its standard hostile mobs (ZOMBIE); a broad, fair reference.

pairs.pair_note: Clear and fair; creepers are more iconic but zombies are genuinely core.

hints.reason: Bowser is the archetypal video-game final boss (BOSS) and Mario's arch-enemy (MARIO); easy but satisfying.
Orwell created Big Brother in Nineteen Eighty-Four (BROTHER) and wrote Animal Farm (FARM); both are school-reading staples, so the author link clicks nicely.
A coach is a long-distance bus (BUS, as in 'coach bus') and a sports coach blows a whistle (WHISTLE); a clean double meaning in the DRIVER mould.
A camera flash (CAMERA) and DC's The Flash (SUPERHERO); a broad, crisp double meaning.
An SUV is a car-type vehicle (CAR) and the S stands for sport (SPORT); the acronym expansion is widely known and gives a small aha.

pairs.pair_note: Modest but fair; SPORT side relies on knowing the acronym.

hints.reason: Chain mail completes CHAIN and mail is the armor medieval knights wore (KNIGHT); the postal misdirect makes it more satisfying than ARMOR.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase join backed by a real meaning on the knight side; good.

hints.reason: You say 'cheese' to smile (CHEESE) when posing for a picture (PICTURE); an instantly familiar scene.
Joseph's coat of many colors (COAT, also the Technicolor Dreamcoat musical) and his rise to power in Egypt (EGYPT); a well-known story with both halves.
Hard drive completes HARD and is a computer's storage device (COMPUTER); instantly familiar, with DRIVE's car sense as a mild misdirect.
A murder of crows (CROW) and the murders detectives solve (DETECTIVE); a well-known collective noun gives a satisfying, PG twist.
Dawn dish soap (DISH) and dawn as the start of the morning (MORNING); brand plus everyday word is a lovely double meaning.
Alice drinks from the DRINK ME bottle (DRINK) and follows the White Rabbit (RABBIT); both are iconic Wonderland moments.
Einstein famously worked as a Swiss patent clerk (EINSTEIN) and a patent office is a familiar phrase (OFFICE); a well-known biography fact with a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect-knowledge hint; the patent-clerk fact is among the best-known Einstein facts.

hints.reason: Fast & Furious gives FAST from the title and Dom Toretto's famous 'family' theme gives FAMILY; the meme makes it a real grin.
The Sundance Film Festival (FILM) and the outlaw Sundance Kid (KID); two well-known uses of one name, neatly linked since the festival nods to Redford's role.
Force field completes FORCE and a magnet's magnetic field gives MAGNET; both are instantly familiar and the science pairing feels coherent.
Jack Frost (FROST) and Titanic's Jack Dawson (TITANIC), with the icy-water theme tying them together; broad and satisfying.
A kid is a young goat (KID), and kid gloves are made of goatskin (GLOVE); the GLOVE side needs the idiom 'kid gloves', but with KID on the board it clicks as an aha.
hints.fix: Kid gloves are traditionally made of soft leather from young goats.

pairs.pair_note: Indirect aha in the RELATIVE style; second opinion welcome on whether GOAT alone reaches GLOVE. The suggested fix only adds 'traditionally' and is optional.

hints.reason: Hair (HAIR) and nails (NAIL) are both made mostly of keratin; a true science fact familiar from shampoo and nail-care ads.

pairs.pair_note: Good; SALON would be a plainer phrase-join alternative.

hints.reason: Tin Man completes MAN and the Tin Man famously wants a heart (HEART); the story detail lifts it above a bare phrase join.
Neverland is home to Captain Hook (HOOK) and Peter Pan (PAN); easy, broad, and it disguises both targets as kitchen/hardware words.
Saint Patrick, patron saint of Ireland (IRELAND), and Patrick Star, SpongeBob's best friend (SPONGE); a fun high-low pairing.
Jam is jelly's fellow fruit spread (JELLY) and Pearl Jam is a famous band (PEARL); near-synonym plus band name gives a pleasant switch.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase join that works because the JELLY side is a real meaning link.

hints.reason: A lightsaber is the popular 'laser sword' (LASER) and a saber is a sword (SWORD); obvious but clean, and neither target is contained in the hint.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; lines correctly attribute 'laser sword' to common description rather than claiming it is a laser.

hints.reason: 'Opposites attract' is said of couples (LOVE) and is literally true of magnetic poles (MAGNET); the two-step through 'attract' is a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: ATTRACTION is a cleaner direct double meaning; both are good and can both pass.

hints.reason: Both a mole (MOLE) and a plant (PLANT) are slang for a spy placed inside an organization; two nature words hiding a shared espionage sense is a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the PLANT sense is slightly less known but solid.

hints.reason: Empire State is New York's nickname, linking NEW YORK and completing STATE; obvious but fully fair.
Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea contains both OLD and SEA; a well-known title from a famous author.
Tolstoy's War and Peace contains both WAR and PEACE; one of the best-known novel titles.
In U.S. stores orange sweet potatoes (SWEET, POTATO) are commonly labeled yams; the text correctly notes true yams are a different plant.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; the targets together form 'sweet potato', which YAM names.

hints.reason: KFC's Original Recipe (RECIPE) of 11 herbs and spices is a famously guarded secret (SECRET); the brand route clicks immediately once seen.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; lines hedge correctly with 'said to'.

hints.reason: Glass is made mainly from melted sand (SAND) and windows are glass panes (WINDOW); a familiar material chain with a small aha.

Treasure Island completes TREASURE, but ISLAND reaches SILVER only by going through the same title to Long John Silver, so the second side leans on the first; PIRATE (pirate treasure, pirate Long John Silver) links each side directly.
hints.fix: Long John Silver is the one-legged ship's cook who secretly leads the pirates in Treasure Island.

pairs.pair_note: PIRATE is clearly stronger. The SILVER line's 'cook-turned-pirate' reverses the story (he was a pirate posing as the cook).

hints.reason: Times Square (SQUARE) and the times table (TABLE) are both instantly familiar, and the math flavour of SQUARE adds a nice misdirect.

pairs.pair_note: A double phrase join that is genuinely satisfying.

hints.reason: A circuit breaker is an automatic switch (SWITCH) that trips when overloaded (TRIP); familiar household knowledge with a neat aha since both targets look like unrelated verbs.
hints.fix: A circuit breaker trips when its circuit is overloaded.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the TRIP line says the breaker is overloaded rather than the circuit.

hints.reason: The legend of young Washington and the cherry tree gives both TREE and WASHINGTON, with D.C.'s cherry blossoms as a bonus link; the Weems attribution is accurate.
